description: Italian trattoria serving traditional plates & apéritifs in a rustic, cozy space.
ownerDescription:

Via Carota is the West Village gastroteca of cherished downtown chefs Jody Williams and Rita Sodi. Inspired by the 17th-century villa in the hills near Florence which Sodi once called home, Via Carota honors old-world Italian roots, life style, food and décor.
Located at 51 Grove Street in the West Village, Via Carota is just one block up from the couple’s other beloved restaurants Buvette and I Sodi and across the street from Bar Pisellino. Via Carota is open all day long serving food and drink, early until late in a true gastroteca fashion.

Live Jazz at Kissa Kissa: Bennie Wallace with Peter Washington, Tuesday September 8th

Kissa Kissa is a Japanese-style jazz kissa and vinyl listening bar in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. On Tuesday, September 8th, tenor saxophonist Bennie Wallace joins us for a listening session and live performance built around his album "French Postcard."

We will play the record start to finish on the house hi-fi system, and Bennie Wallace will then perform live on our covered back patio with bassist Peter Washington, whose credits include Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers, the Tommy Flanagan Trio, and the Bill Charlap Trio.

"French Postcard" was recorded at Sear Sound in New York City on December 10 and 12, 2024, directly to two-track analog tape with no overdubs and no edits. James Farber was the recording engineer, Kevin Gray mastered it at Cohearent Audio, and it was produced by Joe Harley, known for Blue Note's Tone Poet reissue series. The album features Anthony Wilson on guitar, Simon Moullier on vibraphone, Donald Vega on piano, Peter Washington on bass, and Herlin Riley on drums. It is released on BackCountry Jazz, Bennie Wallace's nonprofit label, and proceeds support its music education programs.

Vinyl copies will be available for purchase, and both musicians will be signing albums.

Doors at 5:30 PM, music at 7:00 PM. Free and open to the public. No cover charge.

Cost: Free. No cover, no ticket, no minimum. Seating is limited by the size of the room, so arrive near doors.

Is this a concert? No. This is a listening event rather than a live performance. The record is played on the house system and the room listens together, which is what a jazz kissa is for.

One of the most-requested seats at Kissa Kissa is a corner nook table near the entrance, quietly tucked beneath an original oil painting of a subway rider absorbed in his newspaper. The painting is the work of Nina Barry, one of the bar's co-founders, and it sets the tone for the whole room: unhurried, attentive, a little lost in thought.

Kissa Kissa is a jazz listening bar in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, built around a collection of 5,000+ vinyl LPs and a room designed for real listening. Whether you're settling in for a long conversation, a first visit, or just a quiet drink with something good on the turntable, this is a place that makes time feel a little more generous.

Jersey City's Best Late Night Dining

Hungry after hours? 

San Patricios keeps the kitchen open late, with food served into the wee hours. 

Our menu runs from Mexican tacos and tostadas to hearty Irish pub plates and shareable tapas, all designed to keep you going long past midnight. 

Whether you’re walking in after work, stretching dinner into drinks, or looking for a place that doesn’t roll down the shutters early, San Patricios is Jersey City’s new home for after-hours food, drink, and music.

Cocktails Jersey City

From Irish whiskey and stout to tequila, mezcal, and sotol, our cocktail menu celebrates the spirits of Ireland and Mexico. 

Expect inventive signatures and reimagined classics, served alongside non-alcoholic options, perfect pints, and more. 

And the best bit? San Patricios is brought to you by the team behind The Dead Rabbit, the world’s most awarded pub.

Irish-Mexican for Dinner in Jersey City?

Enjoy Mexican street food and Irish pub classics side by side, with tacos, tostadas, sliders, and pub plates built for sharing. 

Pair your meal with perfect pints of Guinness and a round of Margaritas - and always leave room for dessert.

Jersey City's Secret Lunch Spot

title: Samba Montclair
description: Homestyle Brazilian fare served in a stylish, rustic space with antique pots & vintage tableware.
ownerDescription: Samba Montclair is a small, sit-down restaurant with authentic, well-portioned Brazilian dishes. Yuca, a woody shrub native to South America, appears in several of Samba’s dishes, including its savory starter, mandioca frita com linguica calabresa (fried yuca with Brazilian pork sausage). Entrees include several traditional beef and chicken options, but for those looking for seafood, the camarao na moranga pairs squash with shrimp and cheese in a hearty cream sauce that verges on addicting. “Montclair is a diverse town with great taste and style,” says owner Ilson Goncalves. “I thought it would be a great place to introduce farm-to-table Brazilian cuisine.” The restaurant has a few small tables outside in the front, but they fill up quickly

ownerUpdates.text:
At Samba Montclair, farm-to-table isn’t a trend — it’s a commitment. 🌱🥁

Our chef doesn’t just order ingredients — they drive out to local farms, meet the growers, and hand-select the freshest produce to bring straight to our table. It’s about knowing where our food comes from, supporting the people who grow it, and honoring the journey from soil to plate.

Every dish is made with quality ingredients — simple, fresh, and full of flavor. Every plate reflects the care, intention, and pride behind what we serve.

From the farms around us to our kitchen in Montclair, we keep it local, honest, and rooted in community.

This is Samba — driven by passion, connected to the land, and served with heart. 💛

Samba Montclair – Over 15 Years Since 2010 🇧🇷✨

For over 15 years, Samba Montclair has been a hidden gem in the heart of Montclair — where Brazilian soul, art, and flavor come together in an intimate, unforgettable setting.

Step inside and feel transported — warm lighting, eclectic décor, and a cozy, romantic atmosphere that feels like home. Every dish is crafted with passion, inspired by tradition, and made in a 100% gluten-free kitchen, so everyone can indulge without worry.

From vibrant flavors to heartfelt hospitality, Samba is more than a restaurant — it’s an experience, a story, a place where memories are made.

Since 2010 — 15 years of flavor, culture, and connection.
Thank you for being part of our journey.

ownerUpdates.text: September draws to a close and the last warm evenings of the season give way to something quieter and more deliberate. Autumn dining has its own character - the preference for depth over brightness, for warmth over lightness, for an evening that lingers. The table is set, the music is live, and the night is exactly what fall was meant to feel like. 🌐

The Hudson County dining scene carries a distinctly layered identity - shaped by waves of immigration, by proximity to Manhattan, and by communities that take genuine pride in their tables. Restaurants here are not just places to eat. They are gathering points that reflect the cultural DNA of neighborhoods built over generations. That context makes every meal feel connected to something bigger. 📍 163 14th St, Hoboken, NJ 07030

What does it mean when a restaurant describes its pasta as house-made? It means the dough was prepared in the kitchen using raw ingredients - typically semolina or all-purpose flour, eggs, and sometimes olive oil - rather than sourced from a commercial distributor. The texture and bite of freshly made pasta differ noticeably from dried alternatives, particularly in how it holds sauce.

Fun fact: oysters have been a part of the northeastern American dining tradition since long before the modern restaurant industry existed. New York Harbor was once one of the most productive oyster grounds in the world, supplying raw bars up and down the Atlantic seaboard. That regional connection to fresh shellfish remains a cultural touchstone in area cuisine.

Fall is the season when the restaurant industry traditionally sees a meaningful shift in dining behavior. Guests move from lighter warm-weather meals toward heartier, richer fare. Reservations for special occasions begin to increase as the end of the year approaches. The rhythm of a dining room changes perceptibly when the temperatures drop and evenings arrive earlier.

Private dining rooms have become one of the most sought-after features in upscale restaurants. Whether for a milestone birthday, a corporate dinner, or a rehearsal gathering, an exclusive room offers something the main dining floor cannot - the ability to control the pace, the atmosphere, and the intimacy of the entire event from start to finish.

Wine selection can feel overwhelming in a fine dining setting, but a few basic principles simplify the process. Full-bodied reds with higher tannins tend to complement the richness of grilled red meat. Lighter whites and sparkling wines work well alongside seafood and delicate preparations. When in doubt, ask - that guidance is exactly what the service team is there to provide. ☎️

There is something quietly satisfying about a neighborhood restaurant that has outlasted trends. While dining concepts come and go, the places that endure do so because they committed to something real - a consistent experience, a loyal staff, and a community that chose to make it their own. Longevity in the restaurant industry is never accidental.

Myth: a well-done steak has no place in a quality steakhouse. Fact: a skilled kitchen can produce a well-done cut that retains moisture through proper technique - including lower, slower heat application and resting time. Guest preference always guides temperature, and respecting that preference is a mark of professional hospitality, not a compromise.

How does aging affect beef flavor? During the aging process, natural enzymes in the muscle break down proteins and connective tissue, tenderizing the meat. Dry-aging also allows moisture to evaporate, concentrating the beefy flavor into a denser, more complex profile. The result is a cut that tastes fundamentally different from one served fresh.

ownerUpdates.text: Our Vegan Miso Ginger Ramen is the perfect bowl for the soup season!

If you've ever asked us " What do you recommend?" then this one's for you.
Here's your guide to Tonchin's signature ramen!

Tonchinette was made so that authentic Japanese ramen can be enjoyed more casually and conveniently as a part of everyday life. 
Pick it up on your lunch break, bring it back to the office, or take it to the park. The same quality ramen, with homemade noodles and broths made from scratch, ready wherever you are.

Tonchinette is now open at Shaver Hall!

We wanted to make the simple joy of our award-winning ramen heritage even more accessible for your everyday cravings. So, we created Tonchinette– a casual neighborhood spot located right inside the brand-new Shaver Hall. No fuss, just a welcoming space to drop by for a quick bite or grab convenient takeout on the go.

Just like at Tonchin, our rich broths are simmered from scratch, and our signature noodles are crafted fresh in-house every single day. Alongside exclusive new dishes and favorites like our crispy Tebasaki, we’re serving up our beloved Tonkotsu and Vegan Miso with a brand-new twist. To perfect the quick, easy neighborhood bite, Tonchinette features fresh, straight, thin ramen noodles– a deliberate contrast to Tonchin’s wavy, chewy style. 

We can’t wait to see you at Tonchinette!

Something new is cooking... in one of the busiest corners of Manhattan, we are bringing a space that blends authentic Japanese ramen with the energy of a lively, approachable neighborhood spot. Introducing our sister brand, Tonchinette, opening June 26 at Shaver Hall.

Look forward to the same exceptional bowl of ramen with a twist, our beloved tebasaki, as well as several new dishes created exclusively for this location. No fuss– just a welcoming space to drop by alone or gather with friends and family.
The iykyk apetizer that is loved by our regulars.

Our Tokyo Tonkotsu broth focuses on freshness and is prepared from scratch every morning. It is a lighter iteration inspired by the classic, dashi-based Tokyo-style broths. Simmered over time, the result is a deeply flavorful, satiating broth with layers of flavors that is rich in umami.

In Japan, the arrival of summer is always indirectly informed by a flag that says 「冷やし中華はじめました」which means "We now offer Hiyashi Chuka for the year."
Hiyashi Chuka is a traditional Japanese cold noodle dish that a lot of noodle shops offer only during summer. It holds almost a sentimental feeling for us when we see that flag on a street waving in the hot breeze. 
Summer is here. We prepared this dish in the most traditional, original way as much as possible. Come have some Hiyashi Chuka at Tonchin that will make you feel like you're transported back to that one summer day in Japan. Available at Tonchin New York and Brooklyn all day, every day until September 7th.

This Saturday, September 12, we open early for Bournemouth vs Brentford, kickoff at 10am. Walk-ins only, no reservations, so come ahead of the whistle for a seat near the screens.

When Saturday nights call for live music.  We have been playing live music 7 nights a week for over 40 years, and we are not slowing down. 
Expect rock, blues, soul, and funk from real working musicians, not a jukebox. 
Music starts at 7pm so get down early. 

A cover applies Friday and Saturday nights. 
Walk in any time, no reservation needed, though tables for six or more are worth booking ahead.

Where Bleecker Street does Happy Hour! From 4-7 Monday through Friday, is happy hour at The Red Lion. 
Draft beer, mixed well drinks, house wine, and our Red Lion Mule or Margarita, all at happy hour pricing. 

Tonight there's no cover, and the band starts warming up right as happy hour winds down. 

Walk in any time, no reservation needed.

Two days to kickoff. The Premier League returns Friday, and Brentford open their season at home to Tottenham on Saturday at 12:30pm, right here on our screens. 

We have been the Bees' official NYC home since their first ever top flight match in 2021, and doors open early all season for every kickoff. 
Walk in, grab a seat, the match will already be on.

You can not beat Thursdays on Bleecker street. Thursday starts with happy hour and ends with a full band on stage till 4 am. 
The pours keep flowing all night, and the room shifts as the first set begins on stage at 7pm.
 
No cover, no reservation needed, just show up and rock out. 

Check out the full list of acts tonight and every night. See you all later.

Weekend mornings on Bleecker Street can't be beat! Start with Bottomless Brunch, 10-3pm, ninety minutes of unlimited mimosas and Bloody Marys, plus Red Lion drafts, with any entree. 
Walk in, grab a table, and stick around for the band later if you are still going. No reservation needed and no cover before the evening lineup starts. 

We are a short walk from Washington Square Park and the West 4th Street subway, right in the heart of the West Village.

ownerDescription:
Located in New York City, Cantina Rooftop is a colorful, year-round restaurant and lounge serving Mexican cuisine by Celebrity Chef Saul Montiel. The menu blends traditional flavors with new, innovative dishes, creating an exciting culinary experience in a festive setting.

Featuring a climate-controlled retractable rooftop and an indoor Garden Room, Cantina Rooftop is the perfect destination in any season. Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion or simply enjoying a night out with friends and family, the live DJs, vibrant ambiance, signature cocktails and bold flavors make every visit unforgettable.

Eat. Drink. Vibe. All year long at Cantina Rooftop.
